title: Starting the School Day
summary: You are teaching English to a primary school class. It is a normal school morning. Your task is to greet the pupils, check attendance and organise the beginning of the lesson.

steps.title: Greeting the Class
opening: It is 9:00 a.m. You enter the classroom. The pupils are sitting at their desks. Some are looking at the board, while others are preparing their notebooks.
The pupils notice you and wait for the lesson to begin.
steps.question: What would you say first?

reaction.speaker: class
reaction.text: Good morning, teacher!

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils greet you together and look towards the front of the classroom.

choices.feedback: An appropriate morning greeting addressed to the whole class.

reaction.speaker: maria
reaction.text: I'm fine, thank you!

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: A few other pupils smile and look towards you.

choices.feedback: A friendly conversational opener, but less appropriate than greeting the whole class first.

choices.text: I think we can start now.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils stop preparing their notebooks and look towards you.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: They wait for further instructions.

transition: You walk to your desk and open the attendance register.
You notice that Anna's desk is empty.

steps.title: Checking Attendance
opening: Anna is not at her desk. You have not yet confirmed whether she is absent today.
You want to check attendance before making a note in the register.
steps.question: What would you say?

reaction.speaker: maria
reaction.text: Anna is absent today.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: You find Anna's name in the register and mark her absence.

choices.feedback: The question identifies who is absent today.

choices.text: What's the matter with Anna today?

reaction.speaker: maria
reaction.text: Anna isn't here today. I don't know why.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: You confirm that Anna is absent and mark her absence in the register.

choices.feedback: This assumes something is wrong with Anna rather than neutrally checking attendance.

choices.text: Why were you absent last Friday, Anton?

reaction.speaker: anton
reaction.text: I was here last Friday.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: You return to the register. Maria notices that you are checking attendance.

reaction.speaker: maria
reaction.text: Anna is absent today.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: You mark Anna's absence.

choices.feedback: A question about last Friday does not establish today's attendance.

transition: You finish checking attendance and close the register.
The pupils are sitting quietly. A few are putting their notebooks and pencil cases in order.

steps.title: Getting Ready
opening: The attendance check is complete. The pupils are looking towards the front of the classroom.
Before beginning the lesson, you want to check whether everyone is ready.
steps.question: What would you say?

choices.text: I think we can start now.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils turn towards you. Maria finishes putting her pencil case away.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The class prepares to begin, although you have not directly checked everyone's readiness.

choices.feedback: The teacher starts moving forward without directly checking readiness.

reaction.speaker: class
reaction.text: Yes, we're ready!

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils look towards you, ready to begin.

choices.feedback: Directly checks whether everyone is ready.

choices.text: I'm waiting for you to be quiet.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils look towards you. Nobody is talking.

reaction.speaker: maria
reaction.text: We're quiet, teacher.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: You notice that the class is already paying attention.

choices.feedback: The class is already quiet, so the warning is unnecessary.

transition: The classroom is quiet, and all pupils are ready for the lesson.

steps.title: Beginning the Lesson
opening: The organisational part of the lesson is complete. You have checked attendance, and the class is ready.
You want to officially begin today's English lesson.
steps.question: What would you say?

choices.text: Settle down now so we can start.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils remain seated quietly.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: They look towards you, waiting for the first activity.

choices.feedback: The class is already settled; no disciplinary prompt is needed.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils turn their attention towards the board.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: They are ready to follow your first instruction.

choices.feedback: Clearly signals the official start of the lesson.

reaction.speaker: class
reaction.text: Yes, teacher!

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils confirm their readiness once again and wait for you to continue.

choices.feedback: A reasonable question, but readiness has already been established.

final: You turn towards the board and introduce the first learning activity.
